text:
alex: Heads-up — our Azure Marketplace reported a discrepancy for Feb usage import. 2 customers show negative deltas in the CSV we pulled from the portal. Anyone seen this pattern before?

mina: Ugh. Which file? Are these committed offers or meter-based?

alex: meter-based, monthly usage. CSV name: azure_usage_2026-02-28.csv (I uploaded to /partnerships/marketplace/incoming). Negative deltas in 'usage_change' column.

chris: Could be a timezone/reporting window bug where daily rollups overlap. Azure sometimes emits adjustments as negative rows. Do we have reconciliation logic that coalesces adjustments?

jen: We do, but only in billing pipeline if the invoice_id is present. For pure metering rows we just sum by (customer_id, meter_name, period). If an adjustment comes without invoice_id it can flip totals.

sam: marketplace-bot: import job 2026-02-28-02 finished. rows=12,345, errors=3. linked_file=azure_usage_2026-02-28.csv

alex: @jen @chris would that explain 2 customers having net negative usage after our standard sum? Example payload snippet from CSV:```customer_id, meter_name, period_start, period_end, quantity, change_type, adjust_reference
CUST-337,token-gen,2026-02-01,2026-02-28, -120,adjustment,ADJ-998```

chris: Yeah that looks like an explicit adjustment row. We need to treat change_type=adjustment differently: apply to prior period ledger rather than sum into current.

mina: Do Azure docs mention adjustment semantics? I remember there's an "adjustment" flag but not always documented. Link?

alex: Found this in the marketplace API notes: https://learn.microsoft.com/marketplace/usage-adjustments (sharing) — says adjustments reference previous records via reference id but not guaranteed.

jen: For reconciliation we should: 1) Detect adjustment rows 2) If adjust_reference present, map to original usage and update that ledger entry 3) If missing reference, create a contra-entry in the previous billing period and flag for finance review.

sam: marketplace-bot: queued task reconcile/azure/2026-02 for processing. progress=0%

chris: Implementation detail: our import currently normalizes by period_end; change to materialize row_type (usage|adjustment) and keep original CSV metadata. Then run a post-process step that replays adjustments. That keeps audit trail.

mina: Agreed. Also we should surface an alerts dashboard when net negative per-customer > 5% of prior month usage, to catch large adjustments quickly.

alex: Good call. Can we do a quick patch so Feb isn't billed incorrectly? This week is critical — partners renew first week of March.

jen: I'll push a hotfix to the reconciliation job: treat negative quantity with change_type=adjustment as a pointer to previous ledger. If no pointer, emit a ticket to finance and create a contra-entry in prior period. Will tag you in PR.

alex: Thanks. Also can we add a small note to partner-runbook about how marketplace adjustments appear differently across providers (AWS vs Azure vs GCP)? Partners keep asking why totals differ between vendor portal and our billed usage.

chris: I'll draft a short blurb for the runbook and add samples from Azure and GCP.

sam: marketplace-bot: reconcile/azure/2026-02 progress=40% (applied 8 adjustment rows)

mina: FYI — storage of adjust_reference should be indexed in our ledger DB to speed lookups during replay. Otherwise replay is O(n^2) for big files.

jen: Good call. I'll add the index and a migration script. PR incoming in ~2 hours.

alex: Once fixed, can we run reconciliation for affected customers and open credits if net negative is > $1? Finance asked for an automated credit suggestion list.

chris: We'll output a CSV of candidate credits with columns: customer_id, prior_amount, adjusted_amount, suggested_credit, reason_code, source_file. That should be easy to hand to finance.

alex: Great. Thanks team — please ping if any API rate limits or portal export quirks show up. Will follow up with partners after reconciliation completes. :thumbsup:
